newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Bank of Scotland profits to rise.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Bank of Scotland profits to rise.

text.p: Bank of Scotland looks set to post a substantial profit rise when it announces its results for the year to the end of February next Wednesday, based on continuing growth in market share.

After reporting pre-tax profits of 545 million stg in the previous year, banking analysts expect Bank of Scotland to raise the figure for the latest year to between 640 and 660 million stg with the majority going for a number at the higher end of the range.
A dividend of around 8.0 or slightly over is expected, compared to 6.85p per share the previous year.
Lehman Brothers banking analyst Law recently raised Bank of Scotland to "outperform" from "neutral" saying the group looks ideally positioned to benefit from the growth in direct banking.
Law sees Bank of Scotland's lending volumes rising by about 12 percent, around double the growth seen at its rivals, accompanied by relatively stable margins.
Cost control is a feature of concern to some analysts with improvements in the bank's cost/income ration being achieved by higher income rather than the cost control seen at some other banks.

Since the placing of Standard Life's 30 percent stake in Bank of Scotland last year, bid speculation has largely disappeared from the shares given that the shares were not bought by a potential bidder.
Analysts expect Bank of Scotland to reiterate its strategy of organic growth although the purchase of some life assurance capability could be a possibility.
